title: Economics
description: ICSE Class IX Economics: the six prescribed units — basic concepts, types of economies, economic problems, a study of the Indian economy, poverty and unemployment, and reforms and emerging trends.

syllabusBaselines.source: CISCE ICSE Economics syllabus for the 2026-27 session, as reproduced by Shaalaa and Jagran Josh (cisce.org PDFs returned 403 and were not retrievable).
syllabusBaselines.note: Structure registered from reproduced CISCE syllabus documents; the reported paper is two hours carrying 80 marks with 20 marks internal assessment. All thirteen chapter listings are published: boardprep-schema content was authored against this syllabus, schema-validated and depth-checked before publication.

sections.title: Economics
sections.description: Six units from basic concepts to emerging trends.

chapters.title: Introduction to Economics
chapters.blurb: Meaning and definition of economics, wants and scarcity, and how economic activity answers the basic questions.

chapters.title: Basic Economic Entities in an Economy
chapters.blurb: Households, firms, the government and the external sector: the entities whose decisions make an economy work.

chapters.title: Basic Concepts of Economics
chapters.blurb: Production, consumption and the vocabulary of economic discussion at Class IX level.

chapters.title: Types of Economies
chapters.blurb: Capitalist, socialist and mixed economies: who owns, who decides, and how each answers the basic problems.

chapters.title: Problems of an Economy
chapters.blurb: Scarcity, choice and opportunity cost: the three basic problems of what, how and for whom to produce.

chapters.title: Sectors of the Indian Economy
chapters.blurb: Primary, secondary and tertiary sectors, their shares and their interrelationship in India.

chapters.title: The Primary Sector: Agriculture
chapters.blurb: Types of farming, inputs and outputs, and the place of agriculture in the Indian economy.

chapters.title: The Secondary Sector: Industry
chapters.blurb: Classification of industries, agro-based and mineral-based industries, and industrial location.

chapters.title: The Tertiary Sector
chapters.blurb: Services from trade to information technology: why the tertiary sector grows as an economy develops.

chapters.title: Poverty in India
chapters.blurb: How poverty is measured, its causes and faces, and the programmes meant to remove it.

chapters.title: Unemployment in India
chapters.blurb: Seasonal, educated and other forms of unemployment, their causes and remedies.

chapters.title: The LPG Model (New Economic Policy)
chapters.blurb: The 1991 New Economic Policy: liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation and their effects.

chapters.title: Emerging Trends in the Indian Economy
chapters.blurb: Smart Cities, Digital India, Skill India and the newer directions of Indian economic policy.
